speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) how many preschools currently offer extended care services beyond 7.00 pm on weekdays and whether this number has increased compared to five years ago; and (b) what specific alternative care arrangements are available for parents who do not have flexible work arrangements, live-in domestic helpers or familial support to pick up their children by 7.00 pm.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Preschools have the flexibility to extend their services beyond the standard operating hours, based on factors such as parental demand and the availability of resources, such as manpower.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We recognise the challenges that parents face in balancing their caregiving and work commitments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For parents who require additional caregiving support outside of the standard preschool operating hours, there are alternative options available.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These include paid and community-based options, such as babysitting services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The guidelines set out the process for employees to formally request for FWAs, and employers to consider them and aim to better support working parents in their caregiving needs.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And since the work inflexibility, commuting costs and the lack of domestic help disproportionately affect lower- and middle-income parents, does the Minister of State agree that rigid cut-off times could exacerbate social inequality?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: To avoid teacher burn-out, would the Ministry consider requiring one's preschool per HDB estate to offer care until 7.30 pm, staffed by ancillary care assistants?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: This could provide a safe environment for dinner and unstructured play without increasing the workload of core educators.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And secondly, has the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) conducted a proactive survey to gauge the actual interest in extended hours?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Without this, we cannot assume that demand is low, just simply because parents may have simply resigned themselves to the current reality and are making career sacrifices in order to cope.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Speaker, I thank the Member for his questions.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I think the first point with regard to employees ending at 6.00 pm and having to make it to the preschool to pick up their children, I empathise and I understand that some employees, some parents will face that constraint.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Which is why I think the emphasis on FWAs is all the more important.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I think we want to get to a state whereby the relationship and the common understanding between employers and employees, as a society, is as such – that we do support the caregiving needs of all our working adults, especially working parents.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: So, I wish to double down on the need and the emphasis on FWAs.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: This is because we understand and we recognise that for the preschools to run beyond the operating hours, there will be additional demands on them, staffing requirements, additional resources, costs.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: And I will highlight that 20 preschools is actually lesser than the number of constituencies that we have.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I think the decrease, based on what ECDA understands, can be due to a variety of factors.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: First, of course, there may be lower parental demand.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: It may be the case, as we have observed, that flexible arrangements is setting in.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: More parents do get those flexible arrangements from their employers and therefore, there is not such a need for that.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: The preschools may also face very real manpower constraints, such as preschool educators themselves or educators themselves having to go back to their own families and their own children at 7.00 pm.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: And I think generally, parents do recognise that too many hours in the preschool is not a good thing.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: From MSF's perspective, we strongly encourage our parents to spend enough quality time with their children.
